author: Autodesk
description: Soft serve icecream is dispensed into a waffle cone
documentation:
## Ice Cream Graph

### Description

The MPM Gel material allows simulation of many new types of materials such as soft serve ice cream. This example shows a full workflow from sourcing the MPM gel, simulation, caching the particles, then finally meshing, and rendering the simulation as ice cream and a waffle cone.

One of the first things to note is the enable_high_quality boolean value node. This drives `if` nodes to switch between two values used in the `detail_size` property of the `mpm_solver_settings` node. It also effects the collider resolution and thickness, which set corresponding values to the solver `detail_size`. In general, the simualtion and meshing is much faster when the high quality mode is disabled. It is an example of building a tool to iterate quickly and dial in the performance of the simulation, then allow pivoting to simulate a high quality version of the effect once the timing and general dynamics are established. It is expected to have minor variations of the simualtions at different resolutions.

The new material property `yield_stress` is the primary control to define the gel material. In this example the `yield_stress` is controlled artistically by the `point_age` of MPM particles. An `fcurve_field` is used to map the aging particles to increasingly larger values of `yield_stress`. This allowed the ice cream to easily bend and curl in the waffle cone and firm up to keep the ice cream supported.

The `construct_cone_collider` contains a novel compound `compute_waffle_displacement` that illustrates the power of fields and how they can be used to create procedural 'textures'. There is also a `cone_material` compound to create a shader with subsurface scattering to create a believable waffle cone. Procedural animation was utilized in the `animate_cone` compound to swirl around the cone to help the ice cream form the iconic swirls seen in soft serve cones.

The `mesh_mpm_particles` and `ice_cream_material` compounds provide examples for meshing and shading the MPM gel particles. The mesh utilizes an incoming `detail_size` value with multipliers connected to the nodes that define the `point_size` and `detail_size` of the `points_to_volume` that create a level set that is then converted to polygons for rendering. This creates a procedural setup that adapts to the users chosen detail size and requires no extra effort when switching between preview and high quality detail.

_notes.text:
The file_cache is set to passthrough.
When running the simulation at production resolution it is ideal to cache out the simulation data before rendering, as typically the render will take longer than the simulation and can be easily resumed (unlike the simulation)

Render settings:

On the Bifrost shape node, it is ideal that one set:
Arnold --> Translator Options --> Motion blur mode: Velocity Only

This ensures the quickest translate time since the renderer will only be able to use the point_velocity property stored on the mesh.

Arnold:

AA - 5
Diffuse - 2
Specular - 2
Transmission - 1
SSS - 3
Volume Indirect - 1

Adaptive Sampling (Enable)
Max Camera AA - 11
